record.paper_title: Ductile-to-brittle transition and yielding in soft amorphous materials: perspectives and open questions
record.context_brief: soft and hard glass DBT framework
record.original_question: Can ductile-to-brittle transitions in soft amorphous materials be described in the same conceptual framework as ductile-to-brittle transitions in hard glasses, while accounting for the dual solid-liquid viscoelastic behavior of soft glasses and the distinction between athermal quasi-static and finite-rate yielding?

evidence.quote: Another key issue is whether the DBT in soft amorphous materials can be described along with that in hard glasses. In particular, soft glassy materials generically show a dual solid–liquid behavior at rest, i.e., viscoelasticity . Therefore, they may display elastic and/or viscous responses depending on the applied strain rate, which strongly impacts the stress response and leads to a key distinction between quasi-static approaches and finite-rate descriptions of yielding.

artifact.category_tag: yielding and plasticity in amorphous solids
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has made progress toward a unified description: a continuum "brittility factor" model (PNAS 2024) unifies rheology above and below yield stress for various yield-stress fluids, and activity-induced annealing studies (Nature Physics 2024) connect preparation to ductile-to-brittle transitions in amorphous solids. However, a fully comprehensive framework that simultaneously accommodates AQS hard-glass yielding and finite-rate viscoelastic soft-glass yielding with predictive microscopic content is still considered an open question in the 2024 review literature.

status_evidence.title: Brittle and ductile yielding in soft materials
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces a 'brittility factor' in a continuum model that unifies rheological physics above and below the yield stress, applicable to gels and glasses.
status_evidence.claim: Partial unification of soft-material yielding via a tunable brittleness parameter has been achieved.

status_evidence.title: Activity-induced annealing leads to a ductile-to-brittle transition in amorphous solids
status_evidence.snippet: Demonstrates how preparation/annealing controls ductile-to-brittle transitions in amorphous solids.
status_evidence.claim: Connection between preparation history and DBT, relevant to bridging hard- and soft-glass pictures.
